name: Acorn Master Compact Mouse Driver (PMFS)
description: An annotated disassembly of PMFS, the pointer and mouse driver on the Acorn BBC Master Compact Welcome disc. PMFS is a 65C02 sideways ROM image, loaded into sideways RAM, that moves a software pointer from a quadrature mouse or trackerball, an analogue or digital joystick, or the cursor keys, and reports its position through ADVAL. MOS 5 has no mouse support of its own, so PMFS is the Master Compact's mouse driver, and the interface it presents is the one Welcome-era software expects. PMFS is (C) 1986 PMF; the annotations and disassembly scripts here are (C) 2026 Acornaeology.

analyses.label: The Master Compact pointer driver interface: a specification
analyses.note: A formal definition of the interface PMFS presents to software (star commands, ADVAL(5)-(9), OSBYTE &A3,&F3, buttons as keys, coordinates and the pointer display), written so that drivers for other pointing hardware can be compatible with it, with PMFS's defects listed separately.

analyses.label: How PMFS works
analyses.note: The driver's internal design: running from sideways RAM with its workspace in its own bank, reaching BYTEV and IRQ1V through the Master's extended vectors, the workspace exchange, reading a quadrature mouse through the User VIA, and drawing a software pointer with pre-shifted images.
